prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universal “best” roofing company for every Dallas roof replacement — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, budget, timing, the type of roof you want, and whether you’re working with an insurance claim. I can help you pick the best roofer for your situation. Below are practical steps and a checklist to find a top-quality local contractor, plus an offer to pull nearby options if you give your ZIP code.

How to choose the best roofing company
- Get at least 3 written estimates so you can compare scope and price. Don’t choose solely on lowest bid.  
- Verify insurance and credentials:
  - Ask for and confirm the roofer’s general liability and workers’ comp insurance (request certificates).  
  - Check for manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) — these indicate training and extended warranties.  
  - Look for a local office/phone and a physical address (avoid transient “storm-chaser” companies).
- Check reputation:
  - Read recent Google, Yelp, and Facebook reviews.  
  - Check BBB rating and any complaints.  
  - Ask for local references and photos of completed jobs similar to yours.
- Confirm warranties and documentation:
  - Get the manufacturer’s shingle warranty and the contractor’s workmanship warranty in writing (length and transferability).  
  - Make sure the written contract lists scope: materials, underlayment, ventilation, flashing, decking replacement, cleanup, permit handling, and timeline.
- Permits and code compliance:
  - The contractor should pull required city/county permits and arrange inspections.
- Payment terms and contract red flags:
  - Reasonable deposit (often 10–30%) is normal; avoid paying the full cost up front.  
  - Beware of high-pressure sales, demands to sign immediately, or offers to use your insurance proceeds in unusual ways (e.g., assignment-of-benefits).
- Materials and workmanship details to confirm:
  - Type/brand/color of shingles, underlayment type, ice and water shield where needed, drip edge, pipe boot and flashing replacements, ridge ventilation, and proper nail pattern.
- Storm-damage/insurance claims:
  - Document damage with photos, get multiple estimates, and don’t sign over your claim without understanding it. A reputable contractor will guide but not coerce.

Where to look for top local contractors
- Google local roofers + “roof replacement Dallas” and sort by rating and recent reviews.  
- Angi (formerly Angie’s List), HomeAdvisor, and Yelp for reviews.  
- Better Business Bureau for complaints and complaints resolution.  
- Ask neighbors or your HOA for recommendations.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated roofers near your ZIP code and give a short vetted list with pros/cons and links — tell me your ZIP or neighborhood.  
- Provide a downloadable checklist or a sample contract/estimate comparison template.

Tell me your ZIP code or the part of Dallas you’re in and whether you’re dealing with an insurance claim; I’ll pull a short list of recommended roofers and things to watch for.
